Path: studio — a shared nav-item URL opens that item | 缺项 (the Interfaces pillar's mirror effect deletes `?sel=nav:ID` on mount, before the app draft loads, so the objectui#2272 deep link never opens nav editing) | P3

## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `priority:p3` · `domain:ui` · `area:studio` · `pm:queue`. Direction: the param survives until the tree has loaded, is applied once, and never enters editing on a read-only package. Both copies of the deep link are fixed together

Triage: lands in `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` (`InterfacesPillar`) ⇒ `domain:ui`.

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-09-29T23:02Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

**Why p3.**
- What is lost is a convenience: reopening a selection on reload or from a shared URL.
- Nothing in the product produces `?sel=nav:` except the two designers' own URL mirrors (read at objectui `origin/main` `1d6a23d60`). The nav item is still one click away, and no data is touched.
- The read-only half below is latent: it is unreachable while the link is dead.

**Direction.**
- **The mirror waits.** The mirror effect never clears `sel` while a parsed `navSelParam` is unapplied and the nav tree has not loaded. The apply effect applies it once when the tree arrives. The finding's first suggestion works; the choice between its two shapes is the dev's.
- **Read-only.** Applying the link reads `readOnly`. On a read-only package the link selects the item **without** entering nav editing, because that editing's autosave is blocked there (the objectui#11124 / objectui#11136 class). ⛔ Not left for later: it is reached the moment the link works.
- **The twin.** `metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx` carries the same deep link (`:805` onward), with the same shape:
  - its apply effect returns early on an empty draft;
  - its mirror effect is keyed on `[type, selection]`.
  
  The dev measures it against the same pins first. If it shares the defect, both copies are fixed through **one** shared hook beside the helpers in `metadata-admin/nav-selection.ts`. ⛔ Not two diverging fixes. If it does not, the report says why.
- **Pins:**
  - on a writable package, a `?sel=nav:ID` URL opens nav editing on that item after the draft loads, and the URL keeps the param;
  - on a read-only package, the link selects the item without entering editing;
  - an unknown id changes nothing (the control).

**Serial.** `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` is also PR objectui#11152's file (objectui#11136, ACCEPTed and open) and objectui#11148's. They are different components: whichever lands second rebases. The dispatching seat reads PR objectui#11152's state at claim.

| item | reading |
|:--|:--|
| the change | Both copies of the `?sel=nav:ID` deep link had the defect: Studio's `InterfacesPillar` and the metadata editor's app page. Measured at base, the new pins failed 6 of 6 in the pillar and 4 of 4 in the editor. Both now go through ONE internal hook, `metadata-admin/useNavSelDeepLink.ts`. It sits beside `nav-selection.ts`, which it does not re-export, so that module stays React-free. It is not exported from the package root. The URL mirror no longer clears `sel` while a parsed param is unapplied and the draft or write state has not settled. The apply runs once per scope and param |
| read-only | Applying the link reads `readOnly`. On a read-only package it selects without entering editing. On the editor page the inspector opens read-only on the linked item. On the pillar the selection is held in state and in the URL, because every pillar reader of the selection is gated on editing. To read `readOnly` only once it exists, the Studio surface's `pkgWritable` becomes tri-state (`undefined` while asking, `null` when it could not find out), passed as the internal `readOnlySettled` prop. `ResourceEditPage` waits on `useMetadataTypes`' loading. The review checked every other reader of `pkgWritable`: `readOnly` is `false` for both unknown states, exactly as at base |
| unknown id | changes nothing, and the param is kept |
| tests | Ten pins in two files: writable, read-only and unknown id on both designers. Two whole-surface pins resolve the package list by hand after the tree loads. Ablations: the read-only gate removed turns exactly the 3 read-only pins red; unknown read as writable turns exactly the 2 race pins red; the wait line deleted turns all 10 red |
| changeset | `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`; `Clause-②: no` (the `?sel=nav:ID` shape and every `nav-selection.ts` export are unchanged; the hook and the prop are internal) |
| CI | head `c262d51ee`: 43 runs, 40 success, 3 expected skips, 0 failure |
| size | 6 files, +685 / −81 |
| closing keywords | `Fixes #11153` only |
| governed | none of the 6 paths is on objectui's governed surfaces |

**Out of scope, one line each:**
- The rail's Edit toggle, clicked while the package list is in flight and followed by a `writable: false` answer, leaves nav editing open with the autosave blocked. Edits are taken on screen and never sent. The dev measured it in a happy-dom mount of the real surface; the review confirmed it real at the head, pre-existing, and neither better nor worse after this PR. **filed objectui#11167.**
- On a read-only package the pillar holds a linked selection with no view-mode rendering, so it is visible only in the URL. **Acceptance notes, carrier: none; not filed.** Rendering it would touch `NavTree`, which is objectui#11158, now next on this file. The seat reconsiders a card once objectui#11158 lands.
